questions.question_text: A boat carries at most $6$ campers. How many boats are needed for $41$ campers?

options.why: Used only the quotient and left five campers without a place.
Reported the raw division result instead of interpreting the remainder as another required boat.
Added the quotient and remainder instead of using one extra boat for all five remaining campers.

questions.solution_text:
$41\div6=6$ remainder $5$
The remaining campers need another boat, so $7$ boats are needed.

questions.question_text: $74$ stickers are packed in complete sheets of $8$. How many full sheets can be made?

options.why: Rounded up for the two leftover stickers even though an incomplete sheet does not count.
Reported the calculation form instead of answering the number of complete sheets.
Added the remainder two to the quotient nine instead of discarding the incomplete group.

questions.solution_text:
$74\div8=9$ remainder $2$
Only complete sheets count, so $9$ sheets can be made.

questions.question_text: $59$ flags are arranged in complete rows of $7$. How many flags are left after making as many complete rows as possible?

options.why: Reported the quotient instead of the number left over.
Used the divisor as the leftover amount rather than subtracting fifty-six from fifty-nine.
Added the quotient and remainder rather than reporting only the leftover flags.

questions.question_text: A delivery trolley holds $9$ boxes. What is the minimum number of trips for $128$ boxes?

options.why: Kept only the quotient and ignored the two boxes requiring one more trip.
Added the remainder two to the quotient instead of adding one extra trip.
Left the answer as a division statement instead of interpreting trips as whole journeys.

questions.solution_text:
$128\div9=14$ remainder $2$
The remaining boxes need another trip, so $15$ trips are needed.

questions.question_text: $116$ cm of wire is cut into pieces exactly $9$ cm long. How many usable pieces are made?

options.why: Counted the eight-centimetre leftover as another piece even though it is shorter than required.
Added the quotient twelve and remainder eight instead of counting only full-length pieces.
Reported the raw quotient and remainder rather than the number of usable nine-centimetre pieces.

questions.solution_text:
$116\div9=12$ remainder $8$
Only full-length pieces count, so $12$ usable pieces are made.

questions.question_text: Two questions both use $95\div8$. One asks for containers needed for every item; the other asks for complete groups. Which pair of answers is correct?

options.why: Reversed the round-up and round-down interpretations for the two contexts.
Discarded the remainder in both contexts, leaving items without a container.
Rounded up in both contexts, counting an incomplete group as complete.

questions.solution_text:
$95\div8=11$ remainder $7$
Every item needs a place, so $12$ containers are needed.
Only $11$ complete groups can be made.
